meta.title: Hebrew A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Hebrew → English (see the Hebrew, recall the meaning) and English → Hebrew (see an English meaning, recall the Hebrew). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. The Hebrew taught is the modern standard language of Israel. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Hebrew, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 266 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, work and study, jobs, clothes and shopping, more food and cooking, the furniture of a home, the town, the countryside and animals, the seasons and the points of the compass, the months, the numbers to a million, travel, health and the body, feelings and character, free time and the festivals of the Israeli year, telling what happened and when, giving an opinion, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing and doing — and the other 484 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Hebrew, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word: every form of a noun or a verb added together, including the forms written with a prefix such as ו "and", ה "the" or ב "in" joined to the front. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed as Hebrew is normally written — without vowel points, in the full spelling — with the POINTED form beneath it, which shows how it is said, and Wiktionary's romanisation with the stress marked (shalóm, katáv). Words spelt alike are separate cards where the level teaches both (שֵׁם "name", שָׁם "there"). The Hebrew Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and the vowel points. The 342 nouns show their gender and plural; the 224 verbs are given, as Hebrew dictionaries give them, in the past tense "he" form, with their infinitive, present, future and binyan (the verb pattern) beside them and, behind the All forms fold, their past, present, future and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 748 of the 750 words, three apiece for 744 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, forms, pointing and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
